title: campus-half landing floor hardcodes the literal 10 (campus volume × multiplier) instead of deriving it like the sibling EXPECTED
evidence:
EXPECTED := i64(stream_entries) * i64(surge.multiplier) * i64(WINDOW) // 2×1×10×WINDOW = 20×WINDOW
	MIN_LAND := u64(EXPECTED * 95 / 100)
	...
	testing.expectf(t, campus_window_spawns >= 10*WINDOW*95/100,
		"the campus half must land: in-window campus spawns %d < %d (10/tick × WINDOW × 0.95)", campus_window_spawns, 10*WINDOW*95/100)
detail: N5 derives EXPECTED from the catalog, but the campus-half floor re-hardcodes 10 (= campus volume 1 × multiplier 10). A data re-tune of campus volume or the multiplier silently drifts this pin — the exact silent-drift class N4/N5 were added to prevent.
recommended_fix: Derive the campus ask (sum campus-source streaming volumes × surge.multiplier) and assert campus_window_spawns >= campus_ask*WINDOW*95/100, mirroring the EXPECTED derivation.

title: runtime usage() string omits the new fold-check subcommand
evidence:
usage :: proc() {
	fmt.eprintln("usage: harness run|save [demo...] [--stats-out <path>] | replay <demo> <log.bin> | drift-check | preview-check | stats-check <demo> | input-parity [save] | palcheck | map-preview <seed> [out.png]")
detail: The fold-check branch (r3-N11) calls usage() on bad args, but the printed usage line lists every verb except fold-check, so the new subcommand is undiscoverable from its own error path.
recommended_fix: Append `| fold-check <prev-hash> <prev-tick1>` to the usage() string so the subcommand is discoverable.
